appraisal_events.evidence: "comme c'était de règle les jours où nous étions allés du côté de Guermantes et où le dîner était servi plus tard, on m'enverrait me coucher sitôt ma soupe prise, de sorte que ma mère, retenue à table comme s'il y avait du monde à dîner, ne monterait pas me dire bonsoir dans mon lit"
appraisal_events.explanation: Household routine on days spent toward Guermantes excludes the child narrator from his mother's evening visit, staging him as shut out of valued company and plunging him into dread.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator anticipates being sent to bed without his mother's goodnight visit, a local exclusion from the family's valued evening ritual, distinct from the accepted annotation's separate focus on his admiration of her.

ambiguities: The narrator's anticipated exclusion from his mother's goodnight visit is causally bound up with the already-scored admiration event (both arise from the same coucher anxiety); it is scored here only because it names a distinct local outcome (exclusion) rather than restating the accepted admiration, per the instruction that the narrator's admission or exclusion is a typical supplement target.

Mme de Guermantes is named only as one item in a list of the narrator's daydreamed pleasures ('l'ami de Mme de Guermantes... pêcher la truite...'), too diffuse and non-interactional to support a distinct scored event, so she was omitted.
Swann is mentioned only as a forward reference to a story the narrator later learned ('un amour que Swann avait eu avant ma naissance'), with no local evaluation, so he was omitted.
Rémi (the coachman) does not appear by name in this passage (only 'le cocher du docteur'), so no candidate event was possible for him.
